issuer: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
title: Matter of ABATransportationHoldingCoInc
text:
Case # G1926491
Date of Accident: 11/30/2017
District Office: Hauppauge
Employer: ABA Transportation Holding Co. Inc.
Carrier: ABA Transportation Holding Co
Carrier ID No.: W338503
Carrier Case No.: 1290WC180500057
Date of Filing of Decision: 04/30/2020
Claimant's Attorney: Miller & Caggiano LLP
Panel: Clarissa M. Rodriguez
The Full Board, at its meeting on April 21, 2020, considered the above captioned case for Mandatory Full Board Review of the Board Panel Memorandum of Decision filed November 20, 2019.
ISSUE
The issue presented for Mandatory Full Board Review is whether authorization should be granted for left total knee replacement surgery.
The Workers' Compensation Law Judge ( WCLJ ) authorized left total knee replacement surgery.
The Board Panel majority affirmed.
The dissenting Board Panel member would deny authorization until claimant's body mass index is under 35.
The self-insured employer ( SIE ) filed an application for Mandatory Full Board Review on December 19, 2019, requesting "that the left total knee replacement surgery be denied at this time and the claimant be directed to reduce her body mass index ( BMI ) by way of participation in a weight reduction program such as Weight Watchers prior to any authorization of left total knee replacement surgery."
The claimant filed a rebuttal on January 14, 2020, arguing that the knee replacement surgery should be authorized based on the opinion of her treating physician.
Upon review, the Full Board votes to adopt the following findings and conclusions.
FACTS
Claimant was injured on November 30, 2017, when she slipped and fell at work. This claim was established for injuries to claimant's left hand (wrist), left shoulder and left leg (including hip and knee) in a decision filed July 24, 2018.
Claimant underwent arthroscopic left knee surgery on May 12, 2018, performed by Dr. Katsigiorgis, who noted postoperative diagnoses of lateral meniscal tear, chondromalacia patella grade 3, chondromalacia femoral trochlea grade 3, synovitis suprapatellar space, medial suprapatellar plica, and chondromalacia of medial femoral condyle grade 3.
Dr. Katsigiorgis submitted a C-4AUTH (Attending Doctor's Request for Authorization and Insurer's Response) on March 14, 2019, requesting authorization to perform a left total knee replacement surgery, and attached several medical reports in support of the request. In a March 7, 2019, report, Dr. Katsigiorgis stated that "X-rays of the left knee reveal degenerative changes with narrowing of the joint space, medial, lateral and patellofemoral joints." In a March 7, 2019, report, Dr. Katsigiorgis stated that claimant was five foot six inches tall and weighed 250 pounds. Examination of claimant's left knee showed patellofemoral pain, crepitus and swelling. The knee was neurovascularly intact. Claimant walked with an antalgic gait. Dr. Katsigiorgis stated:
With regards to the left knee, she is very unhappy about the pain she is experiencing. She states she cannot walk more than approximately a block without severe pain about the knee. [...] The patient does want to proceed with surgery. I am requesting authorization for left total knee replacement. I recommend weight loss.
Also attached to the C-4AUTH were a December 13, 2018, report in which Dr. Katsigiorgis noted that claimant had restricted range of motion of the left knee from 0 to 110, and a December 12, 2017, report of an MRI of claimant's left knee which showed a medial meniscal tear, anterior soft tissue edema and degenerative changes with joint effusion.
On April 8, 2019, the SIE submitted a response denying authorization for the left total knee replacement surgery requested by Dr. Katsigiorgis. The SIE's denial relied on an April 4, 2019, report by its consultant, Dr. Saleem, which was based on a review of claimant's medical records. In his report, Dr. Saleem stated that the authorization request should be denied based on the Board's Medical Treatment Guidelines ( MTG ). Dr. Saleem stated that "[t]he documents submitted along with this request do not include any physical exam findings, history, area of discomfort, or reasoning for the surgical request. As the notes are void of all information, the request cannot be approved and is denied."
Dr. Saleem was deposed on May 15, 2019, and testified that he is board certified in orthopedic surgery. According to Dr. Saleem, Dr. Katsigiorgis failed to "document adequately any of the necessary clinical reasoning for the surgery" (Deposition Transcript, 5/15/19, p. 9). On cross-examination, Dr. Saleem testified that Dr. Katsigiorgis failed to document an "objectively completed conservative course as far as bracing, therapy, injections. Anything that would validate an elective procedure" (p. 12).
Dr. Katsigiorgis was deposed on May 16, 2019, and testified that he is a Board-Certified orthopedic surgeon. He began treating claimant on December 7, 2017. Claimant had limited range of motion in her left knee from 0 to 110 degrees. She continued to have pain in her knee after conservative care, which included cortisone injections and physical therapy. In addition, claimant underwent arthroscopic meniscectomy and chondroplasty. Dr. Katsigiorgis believed that a total knee replacement was warranted based on "physical examination findings of crepitus, swelling and restricted range of motion; the fact that she had undergone cortisone injections with minimal to no relief" (Deposition Transcript, 5/16/19, p. 8). Claimant walks with a limp because of her knee and uses a cane for ambulation. Radiographs showed arthritic changes which were confirmed when claimant underwent arthroscopic surgery. Claimant was born in 1959. According to Dr. Katsigiorgis, all three compartments of claimant's knee were impacted, and explained that "the patellofemoral compartment...had grade three,...the medial compartment that had grade three, and on the radiographs she was also found to have lateral narrowing as well. So all three compartments" (p. 9).
On cross-examination, Dr. Katsigiorgis testified that claimant had a body mass index (BMI) of 40 and that the MTG recommend that a patient have a BMI of less than 35 before undergoing a total knee replacement. However, according to Dr. Katsigiorgis, claimant's current BMI does not prohibit her from having a total knee replacement. For claimant to get her BMI under 35, she would have to lose 30 pounds, and that given her condition he did not believe that claimant could do sufficient exercise to lose that much weight. Dr. Katsigiorgis testified he "typically will do knee replacements with a BMI of 40 if they can't lose weight because of their severe arthritic condition. I don't see her losing 30 pounds to do the knee replacement with the knee condition that she has" (p. 10). He stated that lowering claimant's BMI might help her symptoms. Dr. Katsigiorgis testified that "[a] lot of the weight that she has is not around the knee, so technically the surgery wouldn't be more difficult than if she had a BMI of 35. Sometimes the people carry the weight in different areas and it makes it much more difficult, but I don't foresee that" (p. 11).
In a decision filed May 29, 2019, the WCLJ authorized left total knee replacement surgery.
The SIE requested administrative review, arguing that authorization for left total knee replacement surgery should be denied.
In rebuttal, claimant argued that the WCLJ decision should be affirmed.
LEGAL ANALYSIS
Section D.2.f of the knee MTG states that "[f]or symptoms not responsive to conservative measures, treatment may involve knee arthroplasty. Refer to Table 8." Section F.2 of the knee MTG provides that "[k]nee Arthroplasty (Total or Partial Knee Joint Replacement) is not included on the list of pre-authorized procedures. Providers who want to perform one of these procedures must request pre-authorization from the carrier before performing the procedure." Table 8 of Section F.2 of the knee MTG (Criteria for Knee Arthroplasty) provides that knee replacement surgery is indicated if the patient has limited range of motion in the knee or nighttime joint pain or experiences no relief with conservative care. The patient should be over 50 years old and have a BMI of less than 35. There should be evidence of osteoarthritis. Claimant should have attempted conservative care including medication, viscosupplementation injections, or steroid injections. Finally, if only one compartment of the knee is affected, a partial joint replacement is indicated, but if two or three compartments are affected, a total knee replacement is indicated.
Here, claimant is over 50. According to Dr. Katsigiorgis' reports and testimony, claimant has limitation of her range of motion of the knee and has continued pain despite conservative treatment including physical therapy and steroid injections. Dr. Katsigiorgis testified that radiographs showed arthritic changes in the knee which were confirmed when claimant underwent arthroscopic surgery. The only criteria under Table 8 of Section F.2 of the knee MTG for total knee arthroplasty that claimant has not satisfied is that her BMI is not less than 35. Because claimant's BMI is not less than 35, a variance from the MTG is required to approve total knee replacement surgery.
When, as here, "the proposed treatment requires both a variance from the MTG and prior authorization for special services,... the medical provider is to follow the process for authorization for special services and, in conjunction with explaining the medical necessity for such services, discuss how the treatment does not meet the criteria set forth in the MTG and why the alternatives indicated in the MTG are not appropriate" ( Matter of Schoellkopf Health Center Inc. , 2020 NY Wrk Comp G1743084). Dr. Katsigiorgis opined that claimant's current BMI of 40 does not prohibit her from having a total knee replacement. Given claimant's knee injury, Dr. Katsigiorgis did not believe that claimant could do sufficient exercise to get her BMI below 35. Dr. Katsigiorgis testified he "typically will do knee replacements with a BMI of 40 if they can't lose weight because of their severe arthritic condition. I don't see her losing 30 pounds to do the knee replacement with the knee condition that she has." Finally, Dr. Katsigiorgis explained that "[a] lot of the weight that she has is not around the knee, so technically the surgery wouldn't be more difficult than if she had a BMI of 35. Sometimes people carry the weight in different areas and it makes it much more difficult, but I don't foresee that."
Dr. Katsigiorgis' credible explanation of why claimant is a candidate for total knee replacement despite having a BMI above 35 is sufficient to meet the burden of proof to grant a variance from the knee MTG in this instance.
Accordingly, the Full Board finds that the preponderance of the evidence in the record supports authorizing total left knee replacement surgery.
CONCLUSION
ACCORDINGLY, the WCLJ decision filed May 29, 2019, is AFFIRMED. No further action is planned by the Board at this time.
